sections.sectionSummaryBrief: In the maamar beginning "Padeh BeShalom," there are two points that were not explained.

translations.translation: In the maamar beginning with the words "Padeh BeShalom"
(which was said at the gathering of Yud-Tes Kislev 5726¹)
there are two precise points that were not explained in the maamar.
And they are:
That which it divides Torah, Gemilus Chasadim, and prayer in a minyan into two categories.
The precise wording "all who occupy themselves etc.,"
meaning that it speaks here about a person who occupies himself with Torah etc., and not about the matter of Torah, Gemilus Chasadim, and prayer in a minyan themselves
(as the language of the Mishnah in Avos: "The world stands on three things: on Torah, on service, and on Gemilus Chasadim").

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The explanation of the first point is understood by first explaining the order of these three matters: Torah, Gemilus Chasadim, and prayer.

translations.translation: A.
Now, the explanation of the first precise point will be understood by first prefacing the reason for the order of these three matters: Torah,
Gemilus Chasadim, and prayer.
For seemingly, prayer
(in a minyan)
should have been placed before Torah and Gemilus Chasadim,
since the main time for Torah study²
and the virtue of Torah study is specifically when it comes after prayer,
as is known regarding the matter that "my prayer should be adjacent to my bed"³.
And likewise, Gemilus Chasadim is after prayer and Torah study,
as per the ruling⁴
– from the synagogue
(prayer)
to the study hall
(Torah)
and afterwards he should go to his business – he should conduct himself with derech eretz
(which is then the service of Gemilus Chasadim).
